reasoning: The PKGBUILD downloads prebuilt binaries from the official GitHub releases (https://github.com/SubtitleEdit/subtitleedit) with b2sum checksums pinning the artifacts. The package() function performs standard installation steps (copying binaries, desktop files, icons, license) with no network operations, code execution, or suspicious commands. All reviewed files (LICENSE, .SRCINFO, subtitleedit.desktop, REUSE.toml) are standard packaging metadata with no executable content. The disagreement was caused by API errors in the qwen model, not security concerns.
disagreement_analysis: The qwen model encountered HTTP 400 BadRequestError when attempting to audit .SRCINFO and LICENSES/MIT.txt, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and found them safe. Both models agreed the PKGBUILD and other successfully reviewed files were safe. The disagreement is purely a tool failure, not a substantive security disagreement.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review .SRCINFO due to API error (HTTP 400)
qwen model failed to review LICENSES/MIT.txt due to API error (HTTP 400)
Both models skipped subtitleedit.png (binary file) - acceptable for icon files
learnings: API errors should be handled gracefully - when a model fails to review files due to transient errors, the tool should either retry or clearly distinguish between 'inconclusive due to errors' vs 'inconclusive due to security concerns'
Binary files like icons (.png) can be safely skipped in AUR audits since they are not executed during makepkg and are typically small, verifiable assets
When one model has tool errors and another successfully completes the audit with the same file set, the successful audit should be weighted more heavily for the final verdict
